The hosted app likely has a broken or misconfigured success-notification path: the Save button may be wired, but the toast is never mounted/triggered in production, or the notification is being suppressed/hidden by styling or missing provider setup. Another common cause is an environment-specific failure in the save request, preventing the success callback from firing, so the "Saved" notice never appears. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

The “Saved” notice was not visible after clicking Save, so the expected notice could not be verified.

Observations:
- The toast page instructed that a “Saved” notice would appear after clicking Save.
- After Save was clicked, the page view showed no “Saved” notice.

The hosting-side app configuration appears to have a navigation mismatch: the Settings menu item is either bound to the wrong route/component or its label is being read from an incorrect state value. As a result, selecting Settings updates the UI to show "Current page: Sign out" instead of the Settings page label. This could be caused by an incorrect href/path, a swapped menu mapping, or a build/deploy artifact serving an outdated frontend bundle. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

Selecting “Settings” did not show the expected page label. The page displays “Current page: Sign out.”

Observations:
- The Settings menu item was selected.
- The visible page label reads “Current page: Sign out.”

The page likely reuses DOM rows or keys by array index, so clicking Item 7777 is resolving to the wrong underlying record and the previous selection (Item 7778) remains active. This can happen when a virtualized list, memoized row component, or stale event/state closure causes the selection state to map to the visible row position instead of the actual item identity. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

Selecting Item 7777 did not update the selection. The page continued to show Item 7778 as selected.

Observations:
- The status read “Selected: Item 7778” after Item 7777 was clicked.
- Item 7778 was marked selected; Item 7777 was not.
